description: Needs a walkthrough before building. Today type_predicate_of (src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs ~607) recognises a two-clause true/false helper only through an annotated parameter, and Kernel's is_* are defined as 'def is_integer(_ :: integer), do: true'. Once '::' is gone: the recognition reads the helper's first-row questions (patterns plus guard type tests), Kernel's is_* rest on a primitive integer/float/... test (design to propose: what primitive, how the guard path lowers it to a tag test, how &is_integer/1 runs), and each predicate carries per-clause specs (@spec is_integer(integer) :: true / @spec is_integer(term) :: false, clause order supplying the negation). 00615 is rewritten with guard-form helpers. Acceptance: no pin rise, full gate green.
title: A type predicate is recognised from its guards and clause specs, and Kernel's is_* rest on a primitive test
